title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is working out the foundations of crystalline cohomology (divided-power, or PD, structures; his conditions (1.1)–(1.5) are evidently the standard PD axioms). Let A be a Z_(p)-algebra and I an ideal of A. He asks whether a whole PD structure can be recovered from the single operation γ_p.

The proposed data is a map π = π^p : I → I satisfying two conditions.
(i) π(x+y) = π(x) + π(y) + Σ_{0<i<p} x^i y^{p-i} / (i!(p-i)!). This is the γ_p case of γ_n(x+y) = Σ γ_i(x) γ_{n-i}(y), since γ_i(x) = x^i/i! for i<p.
(ii) π(fx) = f^p π(x) for f in A.

Question posed: given such a π, can one define operations π^{(n)} satisfying the PD axioms (1.1)–(1.5) with π^{(p)} = π?

A first attempt is crossed out. It was an induction on N, with a case split according to whether N ≡ 0 (mod p).

He replaces it by an explicit ansatz:
- γ_n(x) = c_n x^{a_0} π(x)^{a_1} (π∘π)(x)^{a_2} ⋯ (π^{∘r})(x)^{a_r},
- where n = Σ a_k p^k is the base-p expansion of n,
- and c_n ∈ Q ∩ Z_p^* is a rational p-adic unit.

The ansatz is the correct shape. It follows from three PD identities:
- γ_a γ_b = binom(a+b, a) γ_{a+b}, so that γ_n = unit · Π_k γ_{a_k p^k};
- γ_{a p^k} = unit · γ_{p^k}^a with a < p;
- γ_p(γ_{p^{k-1}}) = unit · γ_{p^k}.

In particular a PD structure on a Z_(p)-algebra is determined by γ_p. Explicitly, in the torsion-free model x^n/n!, with Legendre's formula v_p(n!) = Σ a_k (p^k − 1)/(p − 1), one gets c_n = Π_k (p!)^{a_k(p^k−1)/(p−1)} / n!. This is indeed a p-adic unit.

He ends by asking whether c_n ≡ 1 mod p.
errors: The marginal question 'is c_n always 1 mod p?' has a negative answer. Using n!/p^{v_p(n!)} ≡ (−1)^{v_p(n!)} Π a_k! (mod p) and (p−1)! ≡ −1, one finds c_n ≡ 1/(a_0! a_1! ⋯ a_r!) mod p. Already c_2 = 1/2 for p > 2.

As stated, conditions (i) and (ii) alone cannot suffice for the extension. Over an F_p-algebra they do not force x^p = p!·π(x) = 0, which every PD ideal must satisfy. So the compatibility x^p = p! π(x) must be added; it is automatic only when A has no p-torsion (take f = 1+p in (ii) and compare with (i)). Further conditions are also needed to ensure the γ_m∘γ_n axiom for the defined γ_n. The page leaves this unresolved.
The exponent in the sum must be y^{p−i}, not y^i (transcription and/or slip). The 'π^*' on the left-hand side is just π.

ideas.what: A PD structure on a Z_(p)-algebra is determined by γ_p; γ_n is a p-adic unit times a product of iterates of γ_p according to the base-p digits of n
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of divided powers to γ_p (p-typical description of PD structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in crystalline theory; Berthelot's thesis/book 'Cohomologie cristalline des schémas de caractéristique p>0' (1974) treats basic PD lemmas of this type; later p-typical treatments in work on δ-rings and divided powers
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's own published texts as far as I know. Unsure about informal circulated notes (e.g. 'Crystals and the De Rham cohomology of schemes', IHES 1966, which does not develop PD algebra in this form).

ideas.what: Question whether an operation satisfying only the γ_p additivity and homogeneity axioms extends to a full PD structure
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatization of PD structures via γ_p alone

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses the problem of characterizing PD structures by the single operation γ_p (minimal axioms on π). He sketches the explicit formula for γ_n in terms of iterates of π, but does not settle which extra axioms are needed. These include x^p = p!π(x) and a compatibility for π∘π. A clean 'γ_p-only' axiomatization exists only implicitly or folklorically in the literature.
missed.quote: Si on a une application satisfaisant ces conditions, peut-on définir les π^(n) satisfaisant les conditions des puissances div. (1.1) à (1.5), avec π^(p) = π
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: p-typical descriptions of divided powers (γ_p as the basic operation) are used in recent work on δ-rings, prisms and divided-power envelopes. This page shows Grothendieck already viewed γ_p as the fundamental operation. Mathematically, though, this is minor and largely known.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine but historically pleasant foundational exercise from the crystalline period: recovering divided powers from γ_p. The explicit formula is standard. His mod-p question has an easy negative answer (c_n ≡ 1/Π a_k!), and the extension question needs extra axioms that the page does not supply. Nothing a specialist would find genuinely new.
transcription_corrections: The sum term should read x^i y^{p-i} / (i!(p-i)!), not x^i y^i; the crossed-out symbol before the fraction is a struck mark.
'π^*(x+y)' is just π(x+y), with a stray mark.
'Il serait instructivement' → 'Il serait instructif'; the final bracket reads roughly 'Il serait instructif de voir ce que c_n mod p, pour un élément de F_p^*. Est-ce toujours 1 ?'
Crossed-out case split: 'N ≢ 0 (p) donc N = N' + ps, avec N' ≡ 0 (p), 0 ≤ s < p' (the inequality line is itself struck).
